newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia needs 11 mln kuna to burn donated drugs.
newsitem.headline: Croatia needs 11 mln kuna to burn donated drugs.

text.p: Croatia will need to spend more than 11 million kuna ($2 million) to dispose of tonnes of old drugs shipped to the country as humanitarian aid during the 1991-95 war in former Yugoslavia, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The daily Vecernji List said Croatian health authorities planned to burn drugs that had passed their expiry date in a Zagreb hospital incinerator.
They also planned to buy a filter for gaseous discharge to eliminate the possibility of toxic waste pollution.

During Croatia's war with rebel Serbs and the former Yugoslav army, and the subsequent conflict in Bosnia, international agencies delivered huge amounts of medicine and medical equipment for the wounded and refugees.
But at the time many foreign donations included drugs which were already past their use-by date.
"The Health Ministry instructed health centres to send such donations back to countries that dispatched them. But it was too late to do so for several tonnes of supplies," Vecernji List said.
It added the drugs would be shipped to Zagreb from around the country to be burnt in small amounts from early spring. The task may take years to complete.
